steps.what: List materials already set aside for the puppet.
Construct puppets and ventriloquist dummies and sew accessory clothing.
Use hand tools and machines while constructing the piece.

tasks.design: Materials already set aside for the puppet are listed from {DOCS}. The actor constructs the puppet or the ventriloquist dummy, sews the accessory clothing, and uses hand tools and machines. A material with no id is not listed. The list does not construct anything.
tasks.previous_blocker: The actor arrived to build and found the cloth set aside for a different piece.
tasks.enabler_now: Materials already set aside can be listed before the actor starts.
tasks.still_hard: The construction and the sewing, which the actor does by hand.
tasks.human_edge: The actor can see that the listed cloth is the right kind and still the wrong weight for this head.
tasks.altitude: Set-aside materials can be listed. The actor still constructs the puppet, sews the clothing, and uses the tools.

reach.task: Have the materials set aside, and leave the construction with the actor.
reach.learn: The list can be shared. The making stays here.

evidence.claim: Materials already set aside for a puppet can be listed. The list cannot construct a puppet, sew clothing, or run a tool.
The actor builds the piece. A materials list is not a puppet.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: An actor in a mid-size European company or company of players. A call sheet does not audition, rehearse, or perform. A list does not rank who is seen.
Fields: Material id, produced by the set-aside already made. A material with no id is not listed. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the actor finishes it by hand.
Native check: Use the store the company already keeps. The actor uses the tools.
unknowns: Which materials are already set aside.
Which pieces need a machine rather than a hand tool.
research_questions: What share of builds start from materials set aside?
Which pieces are short a material on the day?

already_counted.description: The actor still constructs the puppet and sews.
The actor still uses the tools and machines.

incremental.description: The actor finds a material the set-aside did not hold.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Saving is listing materials already set aside for the puppet. It disappears when the material is missing and the actor finds it. Constructing the puppet, sewing the clothing, and using the tools stay with the actor.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: List the trick already set for this performance.
Perform original and stock tricks of illusion to entertain audiences.
Mystify audiences, occasionally including members as participants.

tasks.design: A trick already set for the performance is listed from {CALENDAR}. The actor performs the original or stock illusion, entertains and mystifies the audience, and includes a member only when the trick allows it. A trick with no id is not listed. The list does not perform the trick.
tasks.previous_blocker: The next trick was a card in a pocket the actor checked under the table.
tasks.enabler_now: A trick already set can be listed before the actor goes on.
tasks.still_hard: The illusion, and the choice of which person in the audience can safely take part.
tasks.human_edge: The actor can see that the listed trick is next and that this audience member should not be in it.
tasks.altitude: A set trick can be listed. The actor still performs the illusion and still decides whether an audience member takes part.

reach.task: Know the piece that is set, and still perform it.
reach.learn: The trick can be listed. The illusion stays here.

evidence.claim: A trick already set for a performance can be listed. The list cannot perform an illusion or choose an audience member.
The actor performs the trick and decides whether a person takes part. A list is not an illusion.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: An actor in a mid-size European company or company of players. A call sheet does not audition, rehearse, or perform. A list does not rank who is seen.
Fields: Trick id, produced by the order already set. A trick with no id is not listed. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the actor finishes it by hand.
Native check: Use the order the company already keeps. The actor chooses any participant.
unknowns: Which tricks allow an audience member.
research_questions: What share of illusions are set before the show?
Which participants are chosen in the room?

already_counted.description: The actor still performs the illusion.
The actor still includes a participant only when the trick allows it.

incremental.description: The actor confirms a trick the order did not hold.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Saving is listing a trick already set for the performance. It disappears when the trick is missing and the actor confirms it. Performing the illusion, and choosing whether an audience member takes part, stay with the actor.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The actor still builds the puppet and still performs the illusion. A materials list or a named trick can be ready first. The tools and the trick stay in the actor's hands.
reach: Interior designers can have materials set aside, and this job learns the actor still constructs the puppet.
Musicians and singers perform a prepared piece, and this job learns a named trick is not the illusion.
skills_to_grow: Construct the puppet with hand tools. A materials list does not sew.
Perform the illusion, and include a person only when the trick allows it.
role.ambitious_version: Set-aside materials and named tricks are listed first. Building the puppet and performing the illusion stay with the actor.
